events.title: Gelon takes Syracuse
events.text: Gelon, tyrant of Gela, enters Syracuse at the call of its exiled landowners and makes it his capital.

events.title: Hieron governs Gela
events.text: Gelon leaves his brother Hieron to rule Gela in his place.

events.title: Kamarina razed
events.text: Gelon destroys Kamarina and moves its citizens to Syracuse.

events.title: Megara Hyblaea emptied
events.text: Gelon takes Megara Hyblaea, makes its rich men Syracusans and sells its common people abroad.

events.title: Theron takes Himera
events.text: Theron of Akragas drives the tyrant Terillus out of Himera.

events.title: Terillus turns to Carthage
events.text: The exiled Terillus calls on his guest-friend Hamilcar, a Carthaginian whose mother was Syracusan.

events.title: Anaxilas's hostages
events.text: Anaxilas of Rhegion, Terillus's son-in-law, gives Hamilcar his own children as hostages to back the appeal.

events.title: Recruiting in Sardinia
events.text: Carthage hires soldiers across its world: Libyans, Iberians, Ligurians, Elisyci, Sardinians and Corsicans.

events.title: Envoys to Gelon
events.text: Envoys from Sparta and Athens ask Gelon to fight Xerxes; he demands the command, and they leave with nothing.

events.title: A Persian pact?
events.text: Diodorus, writing four centuries later, claims Xerxes and Carthage agreed to attack the Greeks together; Herodotus says nothing of it.

events.title: Cadmus at Delphi
events.text: Gelon sends Cadmus of Kos to Delphi with treasure, to offer Xerxes if the Persians win.

events.title: Hamilcar sails
events.text: Diodorus counts over two hundred warships and three thousand transports leaving Carthage.

events.title: Storm on the crossing
events.text: A storm sinks the transports carrying the army's horses and chariots.

events.title: Landing at Panormus
events.text: Hamilcar reaches the Punic harbour of Panormus and declares the war as good as won.

events.title: Siege of Himera
events.text: Hamilcar beaches his fleet beside Himera and builds two fortified camps; Theron shuts the gates.

events.title: Gelon marches
events.text: Gelon comes to Theron's aid; Diodorus gives him fifty thousand foot and five thousand horse.

events.title: The Selinus letter
events.text: Gelon's riders capture a letter in which Selinus promises Hamilcar cavalry on a set day.

events.title: The cavalry ruse
events.text: At dawn, Gelon's horsemen ride into the naval camp, posing as the cavalry from Selinus.

events.title: The ships burn
events.text: The raiders fire the beached Carthaginian fleet as Gelon's army attacks the land camp.

events.title: Hamilcar vanishes
events.text: Diodorus says the riders killed him at a sacrifice; Herodotus heard he threw himself into the fire.

events.title: Battle of Himera
events.text: The Carthaginian army is routed; thousands are killed or captured.

events.title: Thermopylae
events.text: Diodorus dates Himera to the same day as the stand of Leonidas at Thermopylae.

events.title: Salamis
events.text: Herodotus reports that Himera was fought on the very day of the Greek naval victory at Salamis.

events.title: Peace with Carthage
events.text: Carthage sues for peace and, Diodorus says, pays two thousand talents of silver.

events.title: Captives at Akragas
events.text: Prisoners from Himera quarry stone for Akragas's temples and its great drains.

events.title: Temple of Victory
events.text: A Doric temple rises at Himera, near the battlefield, probably to mark the victory.

events.title: Temple of Athena
events.text: Gelon builds a great Doric temple to Athena in Syracuse; its columns survive in the cathedral.

events.title: Plataea
events.text: The Greeks destroy the last Persian army in Greece.

events.title: Gelon dies
events.text: Gelon dies; Hieron becomes tyrant of Syracuse and Polyzalos of Gela.

events.title: Gold tripods at Delphi
events.text: Gelon and his brothers dedicate gold tripods at Delphi for the victory over the barbarians.

events.title: Hieron shields Locri
events.text: Hieron forbids Anaxilas of Rhegion to attack Locri.

events.title: Anaxilas dies
events.text: Anaxilas dies; his servant Mikythos rules Rhegion and Messana for his young sons.

events.title: Aitna founded
events.text: Hieron expels the people of Katane and refounds it as Aitna with ten thousand settlers.

events.title: Revolt at Himera
events.text: Himera rises against Theron's son Thrasydaeus; Theron executes the rebels and brings in new colonists.

events.title: Victories at Olympia
events.text: Hieron's horse and Theron's chariot win at Olympia; Pindar sings for both.

events.title: Cumae calls Syracuse
events.text: Pressed by Etruscan fleets, Cumae asks Hieron for help.

events.title: Battle of Cumae
events.text: Hieron's triremes defeat the Etruscan fleet off Cumae.

events.title: Pithekoussai garrison
events.text: The Syracusans garrison the island of Pithekoussai, today's Ischia.

events.title: Helmets for Zeus
events.text: Hieron offers captured Etruscan helmets at Olympia; one, inscribed with his name, is in the British Museum.
